identity.name: Mamluk beys of Egypt
alt_names: Egypt under Ibrahim Bey and Murad Bey
Mamluk household rulers of Ottoman Egypt

land.text: Egypt, the Ottoman eyalet: 'Egypt was declared independent, and the pasha given 48 hours to quit the country' (Ottoman Egypt page)

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws Egypt inside its Ottoman Empire shape throughout; the beys ruled it de facto under nominal Ottoman suzerainty.

land.text: Cairo and the Nile Delta after the Battle of the Pyramids, 21 July 1798

successors.note: Murad Bey held Upper Egypt against Desaix for 'a year', made peace with Kleber in 1800 and collected taxes there for the French Republic; he died 22 April 1801. The Ottomans returned in 1801 (Ottoman Egypt page).

land.text: Upper Egypt, Murad Bey's last land, at his death on 22 April 1801

successors.note: Ottoman Egypt page: "After Anglo-Turkish forces expelled the French in 1801" Ottoman authority returned and the Mamluks were not reinstated; Murad Bey died on 22 April 1801 and was "succeeded by Osman Bey al-Bardisi", whose land the pages do not describe, so the dossier ends with Murad's death (request R105).

capitals.name: Cairo
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Cairo'; the beys' seat in the citadel and city.

rulers.name: Ali Bey al-Kabir
rulers.title: Shaykh al-balad, called sultan of Egypt
rulers.note: Shaykh al-balad from 1760; he 'stopped the annual tribute' in 1769. His second term ended 28 April 1772 per the infobox; other historians give 1773; he died 8 May 1773.

rulers.name: Muhammad Bey Abu al-Dhahab
rulers.title: Shaykh al-balad with the title pasha
rulers.note: Took the post in 1773; died during the Palestine campaign of 1775 (infobox 10 June 1775).

rulers.name: Ibrahim Bey and Murad Bey (joint)
rulers.title: Shaykh al-balad (Murad 1778-1786)
rulers.note: Murad returned to Egypt on 26 May 1775; Ibrahim handled administration, Murad the army.

rulers.name: Ismail Bey
rulers.title: Shaykh al-balad under Hasan Pasha
rulers.note: Appointed after the 1786 expedition; end year is the researcher's, from 'in 1791 the two were recalled'.

rulers.name: Ibrahim Bey and Murad Bey (joint)
rulers.title: Shaykh al-balad
rulers.note: 'They were still in office in 1798 when Napoleon Bonaparte entered Egypt.'

correction.text: Egypt after Ali Bey stopped the tribute and 'Egypt was declared independent'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks the state). Neither page gives an area; Egypt's country shape is about 1.0 M km2 by cells, which counts the Western and Eastern Deserts and Sinai, so the settled Nile valley and Delta are the firm part and the desert edge is soft.

correction.text: Egypt with the Hejaz, which Ali Bey 'gained control of' in 1770; Damascus briefly occupied in June 1771 (ledger)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Gained control of the Hejaz' in 1770 (Ali Bey and Abu al-Dhahab pages); 'temporarily occupied Syria' in 1771. The pages do not name Mecca or Medina; the Hejaz region is the researcher's reading.

correction.text: Egypt alone: Abu al-Dhahab 'handed the conquered territories over' to the Ottomans and became shaykh al-balad

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1772-1785. The Palestine campaign of 1775 took Gaza, Jaffa and Acre only briefly (ledger); the pages do not date the Hejaz's return, so 1772 is a bridging reading.

correction.text: Upper Egypt, where Murad and Ibrahim 'fled' while Hasan Pasha 'took Cairo'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'In 1786, Sultan Abdulhamid I sent Kapudan Pasha Cezayirli Gazi Hasan Pasha to drive out both beys ... restored direct Ottoman control' (Murad Bey page); Ismail Bey was the Ottoman-appointed shaykh al-balad in Cairo. The page does not name the beys' territory in the south beyond 'hiding in southern Egypt'.

correction.text: Egypt again after the beys 'returned to Cairo from hiding in southern Egypt and regained de facto control' in 1791

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, through the French landing of 1798: the Battle of Shubra Khit (13 July) and the Battle of the Pyramids (21 July) took Cairo; Murad fled to Upper Egypt and Ibrahim toward Sinai.

correction.text: Upper Egypt, where Murad Bey held out after the Battle of the Pyramids: 'Murad fled to Cairo and then Upper Egypt'; in 1800 he was 'responsible for collecting taxes from Upper Egypt on behalf of the French First Republic'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (request R105): Murad Bey page: "While Ibrahim Bey fled towards the Sinai Peninsula, Murad fled to Cairo and then Upper Egypt"; he "mounted a brief guerrilla warfare that staved off the armies of Louis Desaix for a year"; "In 1800, Murad made peace with Jean-Baptiste Kleber. He agreed to garrison Cairo. He was responsible for collecting taxes from Upper Egypt on behalf of the French First Republic."; he died on 22 April 1801. The page names only Upper Egypt, so the shape is the gazetteer's Upper Egypt (Nile valley and the two deserts); Sinai, where Ibrahim fled, and the Mediterranean coast are not drawn. The 1798 year is carried by the ledger (loss of Lower Egypt and of the rest of Egypt in July 1798), so the keyframe starts in 1799 without a snap.

ledger.note: 1769: Ali Bey declares Egypt independent of Istanbul. 'In 1769 Ali Bey declared Egyptian independence'; 'stopped the annual tribute to Istanbul and had his name struck on local coins alongside the sultan's emblem'; he had been shaykh al-balad since 1760 and acting governor (qa'imiqam) since September 1768.
1770: Egypt's army takes the Hejaz. Ali Bey 'gained control of the Hejaz' in 1770; Abu al-Dhahab, acting for Ali Bey, 'seized the Hejaz in 1770'.

region.text: Damascus and the Damascene, with other parts of Ottoman Syria

ledger.note: 6 June 1771: Damascus falls to Egypt and Daher al-Umar. 'Allied forces of Ali and Daher al-Umar defeated the Damascus governor, Uthman Pasha al-Kurji'; Abu al-Dhahab 'conquered large parts of Ottoman Syria', and Ali Bey 'temporarily occupied Syria' in 1771.

18 June 1771: Abu al-Dhahab leaves Damascus. A footnote on his page: he 'left Damascus on 18 June 1771 to incite revolt against Ali Bey'; he then switched to the Ottomans and 'handed the conquered territories over to them'.

1772: the Hejaz returns to the Ottomans. Neither page dates the return; Abu al-Dhahab 'handed the conquered territories over' and Ali Bey's second term ended 28 April 1772 (infobox; other historians 1773). Bridging judgment, page silent.

May 1775: Abu al-Dhahab invades Palestine on Ottoman orders. Daher al-Umar page: 'May 1775: Abu al-Dhahab's campaign took Gaza, Ramla, and Jaffa'; Acre surrendered to a mamluk naval force on 30 May 1775. His own page: 'Acting on Ottoman orders, he invaded Palestine to defeat Sheikh Daher' (undated there).

June 1775: Abu al-Dhahab dies in the campaign. 'After Abu al-Dhahab died on 10 June, Daher reentered Acre on 12 June' (Daher al-Umar page); his own page: he 'died suddenly of the plague during the Palestine campaign'. Murad Bey returned to Egypt on 26 May 1775.
1786: Hasan Pasha retakes Cairo. 'The Porte sent an expedition to restore Ottoman authority. Murad and Ibrahim fled to Upper Egypt, and the Ottoman commander Hasan Pasha took Cairo.'

1791: the beys return to Cairo. 'In 1791, about five years after their expulsion, the beys returned to Cairo from hiding in southern Egypt and regained de facto control'; the Ottoman Egypt page: 'recalled to govern jointly'.
21 July 1798: the Battle of the Pyramids. Murad and Ibrahim, 'defeated by Napoleon', lose Cairo; Ibrahim fled toward Sinai, Murad to Cairo and then Upper Egypt; Shubra Khit had fallen on 13 July.

region.text: the rest of Egypt outside Cairo and the Delta and outside Upper Egypt: Sinai, the Mediterranean coast and the Giza-Faiyum belt, which the beys no longer hold

ledger.note: 21 July 1798: after the Battle of the Pyramids the beys' land shrinks to Upper Egypt. "While Ibrahim Bey fled towards the Sinai Peninsula, Murad fled to Cairo and then Upper Egypt." The page names no land held outside Upper Egypt and none for Ibrahim in Sinai, so the rest of Egypt is dropped to nobody (the Ottoman, French and Sinai claims belong to other dossiers). Request R105: the dossier no longer dissolves in July 1798.

region.text: Upper Egypt, the last land held by Murad Bey

ledger.note: 22 April 1801: Murad Bey dies of the plague on the way to help the French governor Belliard defend Cairo, after the British victory at Canopus. He had held Upper Egypt against Desaix "for a year" after July 1798 and, from his peace with Kleber in 1800, collected its taxes "on behalf of the French First Republic" (Murad Bey page). Ottoman Egypt page: "After Anglo-Turkish forces expelled the French in 1801" Ottoman authority returned and Murad "was succeeded by Osman Bey al-Bardisi", whose territory the page does not describe, so the dossier ends here (request R105). The earlier dissolve of July 1798 (ledger/10) is replaced by this one.

wars.name: Ali Bey's conquests of the Hejaz and Syria

zones.text: the Hejaz and Ottoman Syria around Damascus

wars.outcome: 1770: the Hejaz; 6 June 1771: Damascus taken with Daher al-Umar; Abu al-Dhahab then went over to the Ottomans, returned to Cairo, and Ali Bey fled to Daher at Acre; Ali Bey died 8 May 1773.
wars.note: The page dates Ali Bey's fall to 28 April 1772 (infobox), 1773 (Uzunçarşılı) or 1769 (Sicill-i Osmani). It does not mention Yemen, Aden or Russia.

wars.name: Abu al-Dhahab's Palestine campaign
wars.outcome: On Ottoman orders Abu al-Dhahab took Gaza, Jaffa and Acre from Daher and died of plague during the campaign (infobox 10 June 1775).
wars.note: Jaffa is marked 'citation needed' on the page.

wars.name: Hasan Pasha's expedition to Egypt
wars.outcome: 1786: Hasan Pasha drove Murad and Ibrahim to Upper Egypt and restored direct Ottoman control, installing Ismail Bey; 1791: the beys returned to Cairo and governed jointly.
wars.note: The page does not describe the retreat to Upper Egypt; the Ottoman Egypt page does.

wars.name: French invasion of Egypt (1798)
wars.outcome: 13 July 1798: Shubra Khit; 21 July: the Battle of the Pyramids; Murad held Upper Egypt for about a year, made peace with Kleber in 1800 and died 22 April 1801; the French left in 1801 and Ottoman forces then attacked the beys.
wars.note: After 1801 the beys survived until Muhammad Ali; the 1805 and 1811 events are not on the pages opened.

certainty.note: The Nile valley and Delta are the firm part of the shape; the deserts, the Hejaz (1770-72) and Syria (1771) are approximate, and the control of the beys over Upper Egypt varied (Hawwara and Bedouin allies).

Only Upper Egypt is named on the Murad Bey page; its limits and the real hold of the beys over the Nile valley south of Cairo under French pressure (guerrilla war against Desaix, then tax collecting for the French from 1800) are not given.

notes:
State Cliopatria lacks (its Ottoman Empire shape covers Egypt); slug named by the me-10-e notes ('Mamluk beys of Egypt'). Scope chosen: the beys' autonomous rule 1769-1798 (Ali Bey's declaration to the French landing). The 1798-1801 phase (Murad Bey in Upper Egypt, a tributary of the French 1800), the restoration of the beys in 1801-1805 and their destruction by Muhammad Ali in 1811 (flight to Nubia in 1812) are not on the pages opened and are not drawn; a gap-filler should open 'Massacre of the Mamluks' and 'Mamluk' (Ottoman Egypt page: Muhammad Ali 'seized power in 1805'). The me-10-e note mentions 'Mamluk beys of Upper Egypt (extent and date driven out)'; that belongs to this later phase. Counterpart 'sheikhdom-of-acre' (Daher al-Umar, the pages call him Daher not Zahir) needs a dossier; this batch writes it if budget allows. The Hejaz counterpart is given as ottoman-empire; the page does not name the Sharif of Mecca, so the sharifate-of-mecca dossier (Arabia group) should confirm. Ismail Bey's reign end (1790) is bridged. Region names all exist in the gazetteer (Egypt, Hejaz, Upper Egypt, Lower Egypt, Damascus (region), Gaza Strip, Jaffa, Acre).
R105 (3 Nov 2026): the state no longer dissolves in July 1798. Murad Bey page: he fled to Upper Egypt, held out against Desaix 'for a year', made peace with Kleber in 1800 and collected the taxes of Upper Egypt for the French First Republic, and died on 22 April 1801; the dossier now ends then, with Upper Egypt as the last land (keyframe mamluk-beys-of-egypt_1799, ledger loss of the rest of Egypt in 1798-07, dissolve 1801-04 to the Ottoman Empire).
